reviewer: Codex development agent; agent-assisted, not independent human evaluation
scope: All 20 holdout source-answerable cases under both methods (40 requests), reviewed after prompt v3 freeze. This is a fixed subset of the 160-request run, not the whole dataset. Additionally reviewed all 40 unanswerable request outputs; total 80 reviewed requests, out of 160.

rubric.correct: Answers the question consistently with the original reference, without a material false addition.
rubric.partly_correct: Main result is correct but additional text is incorrect or unsupported.
rubric.no_accepted_answer: No validated answer; remains in denominator.
rubric.citationSupport: Whether quoted evidence supports the main factual claims; existence of an exact quote alone does not earn full support.

summary: Agent-assisted review of all 20 source-answerable holdout cases per method judged 17/20 baseline and 18/20 grounded responses fully correct. These are non-independent judgments on an author-created, concept-overlapping dataset; they are not externally validated accuracy or learning gains.
findings: Grounded in-4 used the correct SQL condition but wrote 10:00 instead of 100 in its explanation.
Grounded in-26 gave the formal 3NF definition but added an unsupported comparison to the informal slogan.
Baseline in-28 contradicted itself about BCNF implying 3NF; baseline in-36 contradicted its own source about dependency preservation.
Baseline in-40 failed validation and was not removed from the denominator. Exact quote matching did not prevent all semantic errors.

Structured insufficient flags undercounted prose refusals. On holdout unanswerable cases, both methods declined in prose on 8/10 and returned validation failures on 2/10. In development, grounded out-13 instead invented a university award policy; this is a real unsupported-answer failure.
